Estimate the FWHM of a residual random field

Source: R/estimate_fwhm.R
estimate_fwhm.Rd

Estimates smoothness from functional curves sampled at equally spaced evaluation points. The curves are centered pointwise to estimate residuals for a single group. For multiple groups, provide residual curves after subtracting each group's estimated mean function.

Usage

estimate_fwhm(R)

Arguments

R

Finite numeric matrix of curves, with evaluation points in rows and curves in columns. At least two curves and two evaluation points are required. The domain is assumed to have unit spacing.

Value

A single positive number giving the estimated global FWHM, in evaluation-point units.

Details

At each evaluation point t, the local derivative ratio is lambda(t) = SS[r_derivative(t)] / SS[r(t)], where sums of squares are taken across curves. The local FWHM is sqrt(4 * log(2) / lambda(t)). The returned global estimate is the reciprocal of the mean resels per node, 1 / mean(sqrt(lambda(t) / (4 * log(2)))), over points with nonzero residual sum of squares.

Examples

set.seed(123)
generated <- gaussian_curves_generator(
  sample_size = 5,  # number of curves
  num_points = 101, # evaluation points per curve
  mu = 0,           # target mean
  sig = 1,          # target standard deviation
  fwhm = 20         # smoothing FWHM used to generate the curves
)
estimate_fwhm(R = generated$curves)
#> [1] 17.46428
